decisionVerbatim.A_tradeoffs: Alternative A (A_EXPLICIT_COMPLETE_RECORD) exposes the complete versioned RecoveryCheckpoint (moriarty-recovery-checkpoint/1), RecoveryTransition, and ReopenedRecovery directly at the public library, CLI, and test boundaries. Strengths: (1) It matches the existing functional value-oriented architecture in source/crates/mori-core/src/stage/mod.rs and admit.rs (where stage::load, stage::start, stage::resume, and stage::outcome_report operate over immutable program/plan handles and explicit value records without hidden mutable state); (2) It has zero impedance mismatch with the mandatory public CLI and mori test lifecycle, where every operation (inspect, start, reopen, resume, recover) runs in a fresh OS process and communicates exclusively through persisted checkpoint files; (3) It makes control state (pending with full unchanged Core2 Continuation, forward-complete with Snapshot, recovery-complete with site/await_label/handler/mode/boundary), accounting (committed C, attempted_total T, committed_cap, ordered_effects), positive residual duties, and full baseline/recovery invocation history directly inspectable at every boundary without serializing VM caches or private object layouts; (4) Value-returning transitions (resume/recover consuming ReopenedRecovery and returning Result<RecoveryTransition, RecoveryFailure>) avoid in-place mutation or poisoning of an in-memory object when non-normal failures occur. Costs/tradeoffs: (1) Full history and cumulative ordered_effects are carried explicitly in every checkpoint alongside current boundary state, increasing serialized record size and requiring concrete O-TRACE/O-DURABLE/O-IO resource bounds rather than history truncation; (2) In-memory Rust library callers pass &RecoveryProgram and ReopenedRecovery explicitly to transition functions rather than invoking methods on a single stateful handle.
decisionVerbatim.B_tradeoffs: Alternative B (B_OWNED_PROCESS_SAME_DURABLE_WIRE) wraps the paired runtime state in an owned RecoveryProcess struct with constructors start(...) and reopen(...) and methods resume(&mut self, ...), recover(&mut self, ...), checkpoint(&self), and report(&self), while requiring the exact same durable wire (moriarty-recovery-checkpoint/1) and fresh-process CLI/test behavior as A. Strengths: (1) It encapsulates the association between RecoveryProgram and the current checkpoint for multi-step in-memory library callers and can hold transient runtime caches internally; (2) It prevents callers from accidentally pairing a ReopenedRecovery with a different RecoveryProgram reference in memory. Costs/tradeoffs: (1) Because every public CLI command and every mori test step under moriarty-tests/recovery/1 must execute in a fresh OS process over actual on-disk checkpoint files, an owned RecoveryProcess is constructed, stepped at most once, serialized, and dropped on every public operation, adding process reconstruction boilerplate without reducing wire, admission, or I/O obligations; (2) Mutable in-place methods (&mut self on resume/recover) create an additional unresolved failure-mutation surface (whether a failed transition leaves &mut self unchanged, mutates attempted work T in place, or poisons the instance, which depends on O-FAIL), whereas A's value-oriented transitions avoid in-place mutation ambiguity; (3) Providing a stateful in-memory Process as the primary public contract risks encouraging test harnesses to step a long-lived Process in memory across events (as stage_test.rs currently does for Continuation) instead of testing actual checkpoint publication and fresh-process reopen. B remains viable as a later internal implementation helper if desired, but is inferior to A as the primary public contract.
decisionVerbatim.reasoning: Independent ordinary architectural analysis selects A_EXPLICIT_COMPLETE_RECORD (with ordinary_vote AGREE for the scoped ordinary architecture choice only). First, A preserves the existing moriarty/2 and moriarty-core/2 wire and semantics intact (Program, StagePlan, Continuation, StageEvent, StageOutcome, and global base ExprId/site numbering) while introducing a clean, separately versioned companion module (moriarty-recovery/1, moriarty-core2-recovery/1) with per-handler fresh-postorder expression arenas and finite non-Await handler statements. Second, A's explicit versioned RecoveryCheckpoint (moriarty-recovery-checkpoint/1) directly models all three required normal lifecycle states—pending (embedding the full unchanged Core2 Continuation), forward-complete, and recovery-complete (recording site, await_label, handler, mode refund|compensate, and full post-boundary Snapshot)—together with cumulative committed work C, cumulative attempted work T across false/not-taken observations and reopens, complete ordered_effects preserving prior fees and gross debits, positive residual liabilities, and complete ordered baseline/recovery invocation history (with separate guard observations for both recovered and not-taken recovery evaluations). Third, A aligns directly with the mandatory public CLI and mori test architecture where every start, reopen, resume, and recover executes in a fresh OS process reading actual persisted checkpoint bytes rather than keeping an in-memory Process alive or substituting a waiting-report JSON viewer, bare Continuation, or host-computed financial sum. None of the non-blocking ordinary/interface observations recorded in findings blocks selecting A over B; all 12 designated-owner prerequisites (O-ID through O-IO) remain mandatory and open before dependent implementation or acceptance.
